messages.author: 36ec1331d4d5918f
messages.subject: controlling fill colour in barplot
parts:
Hi,

Thanks to generous help from Kohske, Brandon and Ista, I've managed to do pretty much what I needed:

A 4-pane figure (thanks to facet_wrap) showing the abundance of 3 prey categories and "total", along with sample size being displayed in the bars of the "total" panel.

You can see it here.

<http://dl.dropbox.com/u/612902/Turbot%20coarse%20analysis%20by%20Year%20all%20surveys.pdf>

The colour scheme is rather nice. However, for consistency with past work, I would have liked to have different fill colours.

I thought this would work:

As shown in the plot above:
theme_set(theme_bw())
a <- ggplot(thedataA) + geom_bar(aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = PreyNames), stat="identity") +
opts(title = "Diet of 20-60 cm turbots, all surveys") +
labs(x = "Year", y = "Fullness Index")
b = a + geom_text(aes(x=Year, y=0.008, label=Ntext), hjust=0, angle=90, color="white", size=2.5)
c = b + facet_wrap(~ PreyNames, ncol=2)
d = c + opts(legend.position = "none", axis.ticks.margin=unit(1, "mm") )
d

then
e = d + scale_colour_manual(values = c("red","blue", gray(0.75), gray(0.4)))
e

but this had no effect at all on the 4 colours used to fill the bars in the four panels.

What am I missing this time?

Thanks in advance,

Denis

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: controlling fill colour in barplot
parts:
> e = d + scale_colour_manual(values = c("red","blue", gray(0.75), gray(0.4)))
> e

use
+ scale_fill_manual()
instead of
+ scale_colour_manual()

colour in geom_bar specifies the border color.

--
Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com>

Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology,
The University of  Tokyo, Japan.
http://www.fennel.rcast.u-tokyo.ac.jp/profilee_ktakahashi.html
